title: Typed transform combinators and ergonomic shim between AsyncIterable and Web ReadableStream
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: consumers of the TypeScript SDK ask for a single ergonomic streaming surface that works for both web-native ReadableStream (browser and edge runtimes) and AsyncIterable (Node/TS idiomatic). Existing adapter implementations in the repo are fragmented: several small shims in examples, plus a couple of experimental helpers that don't handle backpressure, cancellation propagation, or typed transform pipelines cleanly. This leads to buggy client code, incorrect cancellation semantics (leaked resources), and awkward user-facing APIs when building higher-level combinators (map/filter/batch).

Goal: design and implement a small, typed surface of transform combinators plus robust adapters that interoperate between AsyncIterable<T> and ReadableStream<T> with correct backpressure, AbortSignal-aware cancellation, predictable error propagation, and first-class primitives for retry and resumability. Provide clear examples and tests so SDK users can compose streams without writing low-level bridging boilerplate.
proposal:
1) Introduce a tiny combinator library exported from the SDK: mapAsync, filter, batchByCount, batchByTime, window, throttle, flatten (for nested async iterables). These functions accept/return AsyncIterable<T> to keep composition ergonomic in userland.

2) Provide two canonical adapter helpers: fromReadableStream<T>(rs: ReadableStream<T>, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): AsyncIterable<T> and toReadableStream<T>(iter: AsyncIterable<T>, opts?: { highWaterMark?: number, cancel?: (reason?: any) => void }): ReadableStream<T>.

3) Define a small runtime contract documenting how ReadableStream controller signals map to AsyncIterator.next()/throw()/return(), and vice-versa. Important invariants: backpressure must be preserved (enqueue -> yield, pull -> resume iterator), AbortSignal cancels underlying source and causes iterator.return() to be invoked; iterator.throw() is mapped to stream.error().

4) Retry & resumability: provide a helper retryableStream<T>(factory: () => AsyncIterable<T>, opts: { maxRetries, backoffMs, idempotentHint?, checkpoint?: (item: T) => string }): AsyncIterable<T>. The helper will attempt to resume from a checkpoint token when the factory supports it (via user-provided checkpoint resume token). We will not invent checkpointing for arbitrary models; instead, helper surfaces the pattern and docs show how to implement server-side tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Exported combinators compile with strict TypeScript (noImplicitAny) and include JSDoc examples.
fromReadableStream and toReadableStream interop with Node streams (when using web-streams-polyfill) and with browser ReadableStream in modern browsers.
Cancellation with AbortSignal propagates both directions: aborting a stream cancels underlying iterator and vice versa (iterator.return triggers controller.close/cancel handlers).
Backpressure preserved: pushing to the ReadableStream respects highWaterMark and does not unboundedly buffer items when using toReadableStream.
Retry helper demonstrates resumable flow in example (using a mocked checkpoint token) and has tests that validate retry counts and backoff timing semantics (fast mocks).
Unit, integration, and a small performance benchmark added: overhead of adapters is <5% token throughput for a 1MB/s synthetic generator in CI benchmarks (relative).
Documentation page + migration recipe added to SDK docs and a short snippet added to Console examples.

test_plan:
- Unit tests for each combinator: mapAsync, filter, batchByCount, batchByTime, throttle.
- Adapter tests: convert a small AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream -> consume via reader, assert order, errors, and close. Reverse path: ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable, ensure chunks propagate.
- Cancellation tests: AbortSignal aborts both directions; ensure underlying generator.return called once and resources freed. Use spies for generator cleanup.
- Retry tests: mock factory that throws after N items, ensure retry wrapper re-invokes factory and resumes (with checkpoint token) per examples.
- Stress test: concurrent 50 producers/consumers with accumulation checks and memory profile snapshot to detect leaks.
- Performance: lightweight benchmark (node 20) run in CI optional job; assert overhead <5% vs raw pass-through for a hot loop generator.
rollout_plan:
- Merge behind feature flag 'streams-unified-surface' for two release cycles.
- Publish SDK alpha 3.2.0-alpha.1 to npm with opt-in usage examples.
- Announce to internal SDK users + collect feedback for two weeks.
- If no critical issues, remove feature flag and promote to stable 3.2.0.
- For Dedicated/private customers, provide migration notes and opt-out instructions (old adapters still available under deprecated namespace for 3 releases).
notes: Avoid implementing complex checkpointing inside SDK — surface hooks for user-provided tokens. We don't want to couple SDK to specific server implementations.
Windows & browser streams differ in chunk semantics (string vs Uint8Array vs object mode). Combinators must be generic and avoid binary conversions unless explicitly requested.
Node native streams interoperability will rely on web-streams-polyfill for consistent semantics in our tests and examples. We will add a small helper guide explaining when to use the polyfill.
Keep the public API small: prefer AsyncIterable for combinators because it's composable with for-await and easier to test; provide adapters for user needs around ReadableStream.
decisions: Use AsyncIterable as the primary composable surface for combinators (not ReadableStream). Reason: smaller mental-model surface and easier to compose in TS. Approved by @sdk-team on 2025-01-15.
Expose adapters that are AbortSignal-aware and map cancel <-> return consistently. Avoid implicit timers or hidden buffering beyond highWaterMark.
Retry helper will not attempt to auto-checkpoint: it will accept a user-supplied checkpoint function. The SDK will provide a reference implementation in examples.
